description.p: Natter Den shows WhatsApp Web in a GTK 4 and libadwaita window, with desktop notifications, a tray icon and keyboard shortcuts.
Natter Den is unofficial. It isn’t made by, endorsed by or affiliated with WhatsApp or Meta. You link it to your phone as a linked device, as you would WhatsApp Web in a browser.

ul.li: One notification per chat, with the sender’s picture; clicking it opens that chat
Quiet hours, and Do not disturb for one hour, two or until you turn it off
The unread count in the tray, and on the dock icon where the dock shows badges (not in the Flatpak)
Ctrl+K goes to a chat by name, or messages a phone number without saving it
Paste or drop pictures and files on a chat
whatsapp:// links from other apps open in Natter Den
A privacy blur that hides names, pictures and messages until you point at them
An app lock with a passcode
Several accounts, each with its own session
Closing the window keeps it running in the tray

description.p: Replying from a notification and calls are experimental. Calls use WhatsApp’s own call buttons: in Natter Den’s window when GStreamer’s WebRTC plugins are installed, otherwise in a separate call window if Qt WebEngine for Python is installed, or else in your web browser.
Downloads that save, and a notice before the page grows too big.

ul.li: A file WhatsApp opens to save, as its own download arrow does, is saved instead of dropped
Files keep their own names, spaces included
When the chosen download folder can't take a file it goes to Downloads; when neither can, the message names the folder and says why
With the window in use, a page that has grown past 2.25 GB gets a notice whose Reload starts it afresh and frees its memory
The memory guard counts the page's graphics memory, and no longer takes WebKit's blank spare page for an idle one
The log tells the page's workers still alive from all those it created

description.p: Voice messages: every way sound plays is woken, and the log says how each one played.

ul.li: Sound the page plays through a worklet or a script processor wakes the page's audio, and stays awake for as long as it plays
The log says how each kind of voice message tried to play, and any error, with no names or words
The log notes a sound stream the sound server opened muted or at no volume
The problem report has a sound section: the sound server's versions, the voice message chain, and remembered mutes and volumes

description.p: A start-up that answers at once.

ul.li: A starting copy answers launches at once: its set-up runs in the background, and launches that arrive meanwhile are kept and run in order
A copy started only to answer desktop search leaves 10 seconds after starting if no search comes
A clear message, instead of a crash, when there's no display to open a window on
The Flatpak build has been tried: it builds, and everything calls, the camera and videos need is inside

description.p: One copy at a time, and no silent hangs at launch.

ul.li: Only one copy runs at a time: a lock the session bus can't take away, held for the app's life
A copy that loses its place on the session bus ends itself, so the next launch starts cleanly
A copy cut off from the bus while frozen is ended by the next launch
A launch against a copy that is paused or busy says so, instead of hanging silently
The log says which copy started, and why one ended

description.p: Memory: what grows is given back, and WebKit stops working against an idle page.

ul.li: A hidden page that has grown well past its own idle size gets a fresh page, with its chat opened again: memory that nothing freed before comes back
WebKit no longer drops all its caches and code every 30 seconds at idle: its memory lines now sit above WhatsApp's idle size
The swap the app may use follows its page limit, at most half the computer's swap
Graphics memory now shows in the memory lines in the log
Use Less Memory in the Background is greyed out, with the reason, when it can't run

description.p: A lighter privacy blur, steadier calls, and a dependency check for every distribution.

ul.li: Privacy blur without a graphics filter, and a cover (not a blur) while another window is in front: both cost next to nothing now
Other apps' audio pauses while you record a voice message, and plays again after
Calls: packets leave from their own thread, a network-process loss waits for the call to end, incoming calls are recognised in more languages, and the log says why every reload happened
The installer checks and names every piece calls, videos, sound and the camera need, on Arch, Debian, Ubuntu, Fedora and openSUSE
The problem report lists graphics-driver hangs from the previous boot too
Replies from a notification are confirmed by more of WhatsApp's current page: the chat list's open chat, the notified message without WhatsApp's old markup, and the chat's picture
The page lent to the reply card is drawn, so WhatsApp keeps working while a reply is sent

description.p: Fixes for replying from notifications and for call sound.

ul.li: Replying from a notification works with WhatsApp's current page, also with the window closed (still experimental)
Fewer clicks in call sound after a silence, with WebKitGTK before 2.54.2 and GStreamer 1.28
A call keeps going through short reconnections, with less background work while it runs

description.p: First release. So far it has been run on Ada 26.04 and on CachyOS with KDE Plasma.

ul.li: One notification per chat, quiet hours and Do not disturb
Ctrl+K to go to a chat or message a phone number
A privacy blur and an app lock
Several accounts, each with its own session
Experimental: replying from a notification, calls, and a Flatpak
